title: 1946 Dehydration plant burns
description: At 4 a.m. on November 7, 1946, an alarm sounded when a plant worker discovered a blaze in an especially vulnerable, powder-dry section of the facility. Within minutes, the entire building was engulfed in thick black smoke. Firefighters from neighboring communities arrived with their trucks and hoses, but the starch and dehydration plant was already beyond saving; their focus shifted to protecting nearby homes by keeping them wet. Although the dehydration plant was not operating at the time, all the machinery remained inside, including a new drum dryer and a complex centrifuge intended for a new glucose production venture. The fire began in the old dry houses, which were slated for removal. The building, located beside the CPR train tracks, encompassed 6,000 square feet of floor space. The loss left fifty plant workers, truck drivers, and local potato farmers unemployed. Estimated damages totaled $300,000.
